title: Infrared synchrotron emission in the soft state of GX 339─4 and the mid-infrared/X-ray luminosity plane of black hole X-ray binaries
question: What physical processes drive the mid-infrared (MIR) emission and spectral-timing properties of the black hole X-ray binary GX 339-4 during a bright disc-dominated soft accretion state?

what.value: Physical parameters of GX 339-4 (distance, period, mass, inclination, mass ratio, extinction)

evidence.quote: 1-$\sigma$ uncertainties are stated for measured/adopted quantities, when available ((cite: Gandhi-2011; heida17; zdziarski19)).

what.value: 2010 hard-state WISE and broadband SED measurements of GX 339-4

evidence.quote: Also overplotted are the r.m.s. measurements from the bright 2010 hard state as observed by *WISE* in the $W2$ (4.6 μm) and $W3$ (12 μm) filters (cite: Gandhi-2011).

These estimates are nearly identical to the source power during the *WISE* observations of the 2010 hard state for the same assumed $M_{\rm BH}$, though the spectrum peaked in higher-energy X-rays at that time ((cite: Gandhi-2011)).

what.value: SXT ancillary response file (ARF) developed for MAXI J1820+070

evidence.quote: For bright sources, the standard ARF shows additional residuals, which can be mitigated through dedicated modelling, and we utilized the ARF developed for the SXT observation of the bright transient MAXI J1820+070 (cite: Banerjee2024ApJ...964..189B).

what.value: H-alpha equivalent width from 2021 soft state of GX 339-4

evidence.quote: Using the H$\alpha$ equivalent width $W$ = 10.5 Å reported by (cite: ambrifi25) during the 2021 soft state as a template together with our measured optical SED continuum, we predict a dereddened H$\alpha$ emission line flux of $F_{\rm H\alpha}$ $\approx$ 10$^{-13}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$ at the time of the MIRI campaign.

evidence.quote: This includes all the sources from the extensive compilation of (cite: john24) featuring MAXI and NEOWISE detections (cite: maxi; neowise), supplemented with several other works based on either ground-based MIR detections or detections in the quiescent state, including the present paper.

evidence.loc: Archival quasi-simultaneous MIR and X-ray luminosities of black hole XRBs
evidence.quote: Distances are mostly taken from the recent compilation of XRBs from (cite: zhao23), or from (cite: blackcat) and references therein.

recipe.goal: ALMA and ATCA imaging and flux density extraction
recipe.method: Multi-frequency synthesis imaging with natural weighting (ALMA) and Briggs robust=0 (ATCA), followed by point source fitting in the image plane
assumptions: Point source morphology in the image plane

recipe.method: Extract 5-10 um spectra and light curves, fit median spectrum with a power-law, compute excess r.m.s., fit Fourier PSD, and compute cross-correlation functions (CCF and DCF) across bands
key_parameters: Wavelength range 5-10 um; 1,470 integrations of 4.77 s each

recipe.goal: Broadband SED modelling and physical scenario testing
recipe.method: Deredden multiwavelength data, fit broadband SED in XSPEC with absorbed irradiated disc (diskir), blackbody (circumbinary disc), and cutoff power-law, and evaluate analytical coronal synchrotron and wind models
assumptions: Distance d = 8 kpc, M_BH = 6 M_sun, inclination i = 50 deg, extinction A_V = 3.5 +/- 0.5 mag using Cardelli et al. (1989) and Chiar & Tielens (2006) extinction curves

recipe.goal: Compile MIR vs. X-ray luminosity plane and fit correlation
recipe.method: Measure archival Spitzer photometry, compile quasi-simultaneous MIR (8 um) and X-ray (0.5-10 keV) luminosities of black hole XRBs, and perform linear regression in log-log space
assumptions: X-ray photon index Gamma = 1.7 for energy-band conversions; flat MIR flux density (F_nu propto nu^0) or W1-W2 extrapolation for 8 um conversions

By contrast, the radio–to–sub-mm (RS) power-law is optically-thin, with exponent $\alpha_{\rm RS}$ = –0.57 $\pm$ 0.03.

answer_key.quantity: Radio/sub-mm offset from optical Gaia DR3 position

evidence.loc: On the origin of the radio and sub-mm emission: a discrete jet ejection
evidence.quote: However, detailed imaging analysis of these data indicate that the radio and sub-mm counterparts do not arise from the core position of GX 339–4; instead the detections at these wavelengths are shifted from the optical *Gaia* DR3 position of GX 339–4 (cite: gaiamission; gaiadr3summarycontents) to the West by $\approx$ 1.2$''$, along its known jet axis (cite: 2004MNRAS.347L..52G; mastroserio25).

The median spectrum, shown in Fig. [2](#fig:medspec), can be characterised by a simple power-law with exponent $\alpha_{\rm MIRI}^{\rm obs}$ = +0.39 $\pm$ 0.07 (with flux density $F_{\rm \nu} \propto \nu^{\alpha_{\rm MIRI}^{\rm obs}}$).
Dereddening corrections have only a small impact on the MIRI band, resulting in a corrected slope $\alpha_{\rm MIRI}$ = +0.36 $\pm$ 0.07.

When dereddening the optical to near-IR (ONIR) range using the prescription from § [2.3](#sec:reddening), the ONIR slope approximates a simple power-law with $\alpha_{\rm ONIR}$ = +1.80 $\pm$ 0.15, consistent with the long-wavelength tail of optically-thick emission (Figure [6](#fig:sedfit)).
Bootstrapping the full light curve yields a mean and uncertainty of r.m.s. = 4.7 ($\pm$ 0.1) $\times$ 10$^{-2}$.

We fitted the PSD with a combination of a simple power-law–plus–constant as a function of Fourier frequency $f$, finding an acceptable fit with slope $\beta$ = –1.58 $\pm$ 0.14 (Power $P_f$ $\propto$ $f^\beta$).
The average flux density was measured to be $F_{\rm 2.2\,\mu{\rm m}}$ = 0.55 $\pm$ 0.05 mJy.
The unabsorbed bolometric luminosity of GX 339–4 during the observed state is dominated by the `diskir` model, $L_{\rm Bol}$ = 1.2 $\times$ 10$^{38}$ $(d/{\rm 8\,kpc})^2$ erg s$^{-1}$.
